correctness.rationale: PASS: crossed A-to-agent1/B-to-agent2 is strictly Pareto dominated by swapping the pair. If no such crossed pair, a positive-weighted welfare witness gives full Pareto efficiency. First p A-only prefixes enforce exact one-each consecutive A pairs; since p>=2 agent1 receives A, so all q B must be assigned to agent1. For odd p, agent1 receiving the last A violates EF1 immediately after the first B; therefore its endpoint pair counts are (k,k+1), versus (k,k) when p even. At B-prefix t, agent2's strongest removable agent1-good is A of value alpha, so TEF1 reduces exactly to t beta<=alpha(1+p mod2), while the opposite EF1 inequality is automatic. Monotonic t yields the q bound, with 2^floor(p/2) independent labeled pair orientations. Independent all-allocation dominance and prefix-EF1 enumeration matched examples p2-5 including the known 2+2 obstruction and equality case. Infinite real alpha,beta scope follows the algebra, not the finite checks.
